relations.note: In the Awajún cycle, Ayaymama is Nántu's wife.
relations.source: Auju nantujai / La ayaymama y el luna

relations.myth: Ayaymama conceals ripe squash from Moon
relations.note: She eats ripe squash secretly and serves Nántu unripe squash.
relations.source: Auju nantujai / La ayaymama y el luna

relations.myth: Etsa transforms fallen Ayaymama into a bird
relations.note: Etsa makes Ayaymama a lamenting bird and her spilled squash clay.
relations.source: Auju nantujai / La ayaymama y el luna

relations.myth: Moon-man sleeps incestuously with his sister
relations.note: The woman who becomes Ayaymama is Moon-man's sister and sexual partner.

relations.myth: Moon-man ascends and the woman becomes Ayaymama
relations.note: She marks his face with huito; after his ascent, she becomes Ayaymama.

relations.myth: Anitetepue kills the abandoned children's mother
relations.note: After Anitetepue kills their mother, Ayaymama imitates the children's lament.

relations.myth: The devil enchants cursed children into birds
relations.note: The devil seizes or enchants the children's souls into lamenting Ayaymama birds.
